yt.title: 18 million subscribers. Almost nobody watches. What happened to Shane Dawson? 👀 #shorts
yt.description:
In 2019 Shane Dawson's palette with Jeffree Star crashed the website. In June 2020 his old videos resurfaced, YouTube demonetized all three of his channels, and he lost over a million subscribers in about a week. He still has 18.4 million subscribers.

Full story: "What Happened to Shane Dawson?" on the channel.

Sources: NBC News, Complex, Tubefilter. Thumbnails shown for commentary under fair use.

#shanedawson #jeffreestar #youtubeafterlife #whathappened #shorts

scenes.text: In 2019 he was the king of YouTube. Eight months later, YouTube stopped paying him.
Shane Dawson. His makeup palette with Jeffree Star sold out so fast it crashed the website.
His conspiracy theory videos? Over fifty million views.
Then, summer 2020, people dug up his old videos. Blackface. Slurs. Jokes about kids.
He posted an apology. The next day, another clip surfaced.
YouTube cut the ads on all three of his channels. Over a million subscribers gone in about a week.
But wait. He still has eighteen million subscribers. So why does almost nobody see his videos?
You see, subscribers are like old phone numbers. You still have them, but nobody picks up. His biggest video did fifty four million. His comeback? Five point seven.
Today he's married, a dad of twins, and posts a few times a year.

p.text: HE KEPT THE CROWN.|LOST THE KINGDOM.

scenes.text: The king of YouTube still has his crown. He just lost the kingdom.
